title: CP 124: minimum wages as of July 1, 2026
summary: Set the gross hourly wage by occupational category and team responsibility. The official scale applicable as of July 1, 2026 was updated on July 7, 2026.
body: For the 40-hour regime, published gross hourly minima: category I, 18.592 €; IA, 19.517 €; II, 19.820 €; IIA, 20.810 €; III, 21.078 €; IV, 22.374 €. These scales apply to workers; certain activities, notably dredging and concrete plants supplying third parties, have separate agreements.

The crew leader must receive at least 10% above the wage corresponding to their qualification and the contractual wage of the highest qualification in their team. The scale indicates 23.186 €/h for crew leader III, 24.597 €/h for crew leader IV, and 26.810 €/h for foreman IV.

As of July 1, 2026, the supplement for hours in an active petrochemical company is 0.799 €/h. Published daily allowances are 16.81 € for lodging and 35.19 € for meals. Verify the conditions for granting them before announcing them.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Loyalty and weather stamps: beneficiaries and calculation
summary: Loyalty and weather stamps are distinct sectoral benefits. Students are excluded from this collective agreement; temporary workers covered are included.
body: The collective agreement of September 12, 2013, applicable since September 1, 2013, provides for loyalty stamps at 9% and weather stamps at 2% of gross remuneration at 100%. Articles 2 to 4 distinguish employer contributions from benefits paid: 9.12% for loyalty and administration; 2.10% for weather and administration.

Weather stamps concern companies in ONSS categories 024 and 054 and temporary workers assigned to them. Do not promise this benefit to all employees of a construction company. The loyalty period runs from July 1 to June 30; the weather period from January 1 to December 31.

For a job offer, present these benefits separately from hourly wages. The regime for foreign employers was modified by the collective agreement of February 14, 2019 and is covered in the construction-timbres-travailleurs-detaches sheet.
source: SPF Employment, collective agreement registry · public-search.werk.belgie.be

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Checkinatwork: register attendance before work
summary: Organize daily registration of people working on sites subject to Checkinatwork. Exit registration announced for April 2027 does not yet apply as of September 30, 2026.
body: For real estate work covered, the threshold is 500,000 € excluding VAT for the total work amount. The site must be listed in the Work Declaration. The employer or contractor organizes registration of workers, subcontractors, and self-employed; they can also register themselves.
Registration must take place each day before work begins. On arrival, specify the method used and the person responsible for verifying registered attendance.

The ONSS notice of July 30, 2026 announces the transition to Check in and out at work on April 1, 2027, under articles 124 to 131 of the program law of May 30, 2026. As of that date, covered real estate work can no longer be registered in Checkinatwork. Prepare the migration without anticipating the exit requirement.

title: Worksites: basic safety training and VCA
summary: Verify basic safety training or equivalent proof before assignment to the worksite. A VCA certificate can establish required knowledge without replacing trade-specific training.
body: Since April 15, 2023, the federal rule applies to workers, self-employed individuals, and employers performing the work themselves. Training lasts at least eight hours and precedes the start of work; if prior organization is impossible, it must be completed within the month following the start of work.

Knowledge is presumed acquired with an equivalent training certificate, for example VCA, or at least five years of worksite experience in the last ten years. Keep supporting documentation. Stricter sectoral rules remain applicable, notably for temporary work.
The employer must always provide information about site risks before work begins and verify understanding. Basic training does not exempt from training on machinery operation or asbestos removal.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Weather conditions: temporary unemployment and eC3.2 card
summary: Apply the ONEM procedure specific to construction and train new workers on eC3.2. Paper forms are no longer the standard procedure since January 1, 2025.
body: If a worker begins work and then interrupts it due to weather conditions, they are entitled to remuneration and cannot be placed on weather-related unemployment for that day. If work cannot begin upon arrival at the site, construction regulations permit unemployment for that day.

Report the first actual day to ONEM monthly on the same day or the next business day; the preceding business day is possible if unemployment is certain. Submit DRS scenario 2 when necessary and DRS scenario 5 after the month.

The worker completes eC3.2 starting on the first day of each month, even without unemployment, and indicates work before beginning it. They submit the card at month’s end if they experienced temporary unemployment. Temporary return to paper requires ONEM approval. From March 1, 2026, registration as a job seeker occurs after the first three months of temporary unemployment.

title: Posting: check Limosa-1 proof
summary: Before starting a posting assignment, request Limosa-1 proof and verify the period and place of work. The Belgian client must report the absence of proof.
body: The Limosa obligation has been in effect since April 1, 2007. It concerns notably employees sent to work temporarily or partially in Belgium and self-employed individuals posted in risk sectors, including construction. Examine exemptions provided by activity and duration; nationality alone is insufficient to determine the obligation.

Limosa-1 proof must be presented to the Belgian client before beginning activities. If it is missing, the client must report this non-presentation to the authorities. Adapt or extend the declaration if the assignment changes.
The Limosa-1 QR code can be used to register the person in Checkinatwork. Limosa declaration and daily attendance registration are two separate procedures.

title: Temporary worksites: coordination and prevention
summary: The Royal Decree of January 25, 2001 governs the organization of safety on temporary or mobile worksites. Plan coordination and instructions before assembling teams.
body: Article 2 covers notably construction, renovation, excavation, repair, and demolition. When multiple contractors are involved, simultaneously or successively, check coordination obligations in design and execution according to the site configuration.

Article 26 requires a health and safety plan in the cases it defines, notably certain work presenting particular risks. Article 30 organizes its integration into market documents, with procedures and exemptions provided by the text. A job offer does not replace these documents.

Article 50 requires contractors to implement prevention measures concerning notably access, circulation, handling, equipment maintenance, and interactions between companies. When recruiting a site manager, distinguish their tasks from those of the health and safety coordinator, a role subject to its own conditions. The PDF notably incorporates the amendment of April 7, 2023, published April 14, 2023.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Students on worksites: prohibited tasks and exemptions
summary: A student contract does not permit freely assigning young workers to dangerous machinery and work on the site. Verify actual tasks before publishing the offer.
body: Articles X.3-3 and X.3-8 of the Code require prior risk analysis adapted to lack of experience and prohibit dangerous work, notably those in Annex X.3-1. Renew the analysis at least annually and when there is a significant change to the position.

For a student, Article X.3-11 permits certain exemptions only from age 18, when studies correspond to the activities concerned. The employer must guarantee effective prevention measures, oversight, and the presence of an experienced worker; request prior opinion from the committee and prevention adviser.

Article X.3-11/1 provides a specific prohibition on operating motorized handling equipment, with limited exceptions for certain trolleys and hand pallet trucks. Do not transform the general exemption into authorization to operate any machine. The text incorporates the amendment published June 10, 2024.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Roofers: fall protection and scaffolding
summary: Provide appropriate protections and training for work at height. A roofer’s experience does not exempt the employer from securing the worksite.
body: Articles IV.5-1 to IV.5-3 require selection of appropriate equipment after risk analysis. Prioritize collective fall protection, notably guardrails and platforms, over individual protection. Only perform work if weather permits safe work without compromising safety.

Article IV.5-4 limits the use of a ladder as a work position to low-risk situations where safer equipment is not justified, considering short duration or site characteristics. A ladder is therefore not the normal position for all roofing work.

For scaffolding, organize the designation of a competent person, checks, and training appropriate to use or assembly, disassembly, and modification. Verify these skills when recruiting. The PDF incorporates the amendment published June 10, 2024.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Equipment and cranes: verify operating training
summary: Request training proof corresponding to the equipment actually used. A general VCA certificate does not alone demonstrate operating competence.
body: Article IV.3-7, 1° of the Code reserves operation of self-propelled mobile equipment to workers who have received appropriate training for safe operation. The employer also organizes circulation and pedestrian protection in the work area.

For a crane operator, specify the crane type and examine professional training, the corresponding certificate or credential. The Prevention and Temporary Work guide describes these trainings, notably from centers recognized by Constructiv, and medical fitness related to the safety position: https://www.fichepostedetravail.be/sites/default/files/2024-10/fiche_grutier_et_conducteur_d_engins_de_levage.pdf.

Lifting equipment also falls under Book IV, Title 4. Distinguish proof of operator competence, site-specific instructions, and equipment checks. The consolidated version of the Code used is dated June 13, 2026.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: ConstruBadge: identification of workers on worksites
summary: Verify ConstruBadge issuance when welcoming a worker. This visual identification badge only records attendance if connected to a system provided for that purpose.
body: The sectoral issuance regime results from the collective agreement of September 11, 2014, effective October 1, 2014. Constructiv issues badges based on official data from Dimona, DmfA, and Limosa. This notably concerns workers from Belgian companies, temporary workers, and workers posted by foreign employers.

For employees of Belgian companies, Constructiv sends the badge to their home address. For foreign employers, issuance involves formalities, payment, and a Belgian delivery address. The employer checks issued badges and requests replacement in the ConstruBadge application.

On arrival, verify identity, badge, and applicable attendance procedure. Constructiv specifies that its use to record attendance depends on the capabilities of the access control or registration system used.

title: Temporary work in construction: reasons and conditions
summary: Temporary work has been authorized in construction since 2002. The collective agreement of December 4, 2014 sets three reasons and sectoral conditions to verify before the assignment.
body: Article 3 permits replacement of a permanent worker on leave, temporary increase in work volume, and placement for permanent hiring. Articles 5 and 6 govern agreement or information and consultation of the union delegation depending on the reason.

Articles 7 and 8 require an approved construction temporary work agency and a separate legal entity. Verify the required approval and its mention in the contract. Article 3 requires a construction safety training certificate of at least sixteen hours, subject to equivalences and exemptions it provides.

Article 11 prohibits daily contracts and limits assignment of the same temporary worker to the same company to six months for temporary increase. Article 12 prohibits replacing work normally performed by employees on temporary unemployment with temporary workers. The collective agreement applies since October 1, 2014.
source: Belgian Official Journal, SPF Employment · ejustice.just.fgov.be

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Construction: distinguishing workers CP 124 and employees CP 200
summary: A construction company may employ workers CP 124 and employees CP 200. Verify status and activity before choosing scales and benefits in the offer.
body: The Pensio B FAQ defines construction employees as CP 200 employees of a company or technical operating unit that also employs CP 124 workers, who cannot be assigned to another activity. When multiple activities are present, it retains the predominance criterion. Do not automatically apply worker hourly scales to salaried staff.

The supplementary pension scheme for construction employees applies to employers without a recognized equivalent plan. Affiliation occurs via DmfA; verify indices with payroll management. Since January 1, 2026, the scheme includes a solidarity component.

The FAQ distinguishes the pension contribution set at 1.80% of reference salary as of January 1, 2026 from the overall employer contribution of 2.23%, which also finances components provided for in the scheme. To present the benefit to candidates, verify their actual affiliation.

owner.name: Pensio B et Fonds de sécurité d’existence pour les pensions complémentaires de la construction

title: Posting: stamps and OPOC registration
summary: For a foreign employer, verify the stamp regime and any equivalences. The 2019 collective agreement modifies the procedure provided in the 2013 text.
body: The collective agreement of February 14, 2019 amends Article 1 of the collective agreement of September 12, 2013. The foreign employer fulfills its OPOC registration obligation through Limosa declaration. Check this declaration before the worksite.

For loyalty stamps, the exemption related to equivalent benefits in the country of establishment meets the conditions of the text and the examination by the collection entity. Do not consider a simple assertion by the employer as sufficient proof.

The provisions for collection, issuance, and valuation of weather stamps do not apply to foreign employers and workers they temporarily post in Belgium. The employer remains required to pay the full guaranteed daily wage if the day is interrupted due to weather. The amendment took effect on January 1, 2019.
source: SPF Employment, collective agreement registry · public-search.werk.belgie.be
